questions.question: In the early 1980s, an aspartic acid-containing dipeptide sweetener was discovered, that was about 2000 times sweeter than sucrose. What is the name of that sweetener?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Alitame__.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **Alitame is an aspartic acid-containing dipeptide sweetener**.
 
• It was developed by** Pfizer.**
 
• Currently marketed in some countries under the **brand name Aclame**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Saccharin** is an **artificial sweetener.**
 
• **Aspartame** is an artificial **non-saccharide sweetener**.
 
• **Sucralose** is an **artificial sweetener** and **sugar substitute**.

questions.question: A balanced diet takes care of all the following aspects, EXCEPT one. Identify the aspect.

options.text: Meets the RDA for all nutrients
Includes a variety of food items

questions.solution:
The correct answer is** __Promotes a healthy mind__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Balance Diet**

 
 
• A **balanced diet consists of a range of meals in the right amounts and ratios** to provide the body with all the necessary elements it needs each day.
 
• These elements include **proteins, carbs, fats, vitamins, minerals, water, and fibre**.
 
• Such a diet **aids in promoting and maintaining good health and also offers a reserve of nutrients to resist brief periods of deprivation **when those nutrients are not provided by the diet.
 
• The following **aspects** are taken care of by a balanced diet:
 
 
• Meets the **RDA for all nutrients**
 
• Includes nutrients in **correct proportions**
 
• Includes a** variety of food items**
 
• Preserve and promotes **good health**
 
• Provides a **safety margin for nutrients**
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **safety margin covers the days we fast as well as any temporary nutrient deficiencies** in our everyday diet.
 
• The s**afety margin is already built in if a balanced diet satisfies an individual's Recommended Dietary Allowances (RDAs)**, as RDAs are created with additional allowances in mind.
 
• Taking care that **each group of foods is present in the meals is one of the simplest strategies to create a balanced diet**.
 
• The **Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) **recommends **five fundamental food groups**.
 
• These consist of:
 
 
• **Products, grains, and cereals**
 
• **Pulses and legumes**
 
• **Dairy and meat products**
 
• **Fruits and vegetables**
 
• **Fats and sugars**

questions.question: Find the odd one out with respect to animals’ response to abiotic factors.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Reproduce**__.

__
 
• The factor to which the animal's response is reproduce is a biotic factor.
 
• So, the correct option is** Reproduce.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• There are two types of factors affecting the ecosystem:
 
 
• **Biotic factors **
 
• **Abiotic factors**
 
 
 
• **Biotic factors** are the living parts of an ecosystem that shapes its environment.
 
• Some common biotic factors are** consumers, producers, herbivores, carnivores, omnivores, and decomposers.**
 
• **Abiotic factors **are non-living parts of an ecosystem that shapes its environment. 
 
• Five common abiotic factors are** atmosphere, temperature/ sunlight, water, chemical elements, and wind.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__ **

 
• An ecosystem is a place where the living and nonliving components 'interact with each other.
 
• **Type of ecosystems**:
 
 
• **Aquatic Ecosystem: Freshwater ecosystem, Marine ecosystem**
 
• **Terrestrial Ecosystem: Forest ecosystem, Grassland ecosystem, Tundra ecosystem, and Desert ecosystem.**
 
 
 
• The largest ecosystem in the world is the aquatic ecosystem. It constitutes 70% of the surface of the earth.

questions.question: The bacterium flagellum is composed of three major structural elements. Which of the following is NOT one of these elements?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Torso**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bacterium Flagella**

 
 
• Bacterial flagella are **made of the protein flagellin and are a coiled, thread-like structure with a sharp bend and a rotary motor at the base**.
 
• It gives bacteria the **ability to swim freely **through a binary compound of aqueous, also known as **motility or self-propulsion**. 
 
• It is composed of **three major** structural elements;
 
 
• **Basal body**
 
 
• It is joined to the **cytoplasmic membrane and cell membrane**.

 It is made up of **rings **that are surrounded by **MotB proteins**.
 
 
 
• **Hook**
 
 
• A hook is the name for the **wider area at the base of the flagellum**.
 
• It connects the** filament to the base's motor protein**.
 
 
 
• **Filament**
 
 
• It is a** ****thin, hair-like structure** emerging from the hook.
 
 
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://www.oercommons.org/editor/images/2358] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The long, helical filament of bacterial flagella is made up of **several flagellin subunits organised in a variety of tangled chains**.
 
• A flagellum is made up of **numerous parts and rotates**, similar to a boat motor's propeller.
 
• Depending on the species, the diameter of bacterial flagella varies, which lies between 15 and 20 nm.
 
• **Functions of Bacterial Flagella**
 
 
• Role in pathogenesis
 
• Organ of locomotion
 
• Role in identification of organism

questions.question: At high doses, ______ kills cancer cells or slows their growth by damaging their DNA. Cancer cells whose DNA is damaged beyond repair stop dividing or die. When the damaged cells die, they are broken down and removed by the body.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Radiation therapy**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Radiotherapy to treat cancer:

 
 
• High doses of radiation are used in radiation therapy, also known as radiotherapy, as a cancer treatment to eradicate cancer cells and reduce tumour size.
 
• As with X-rays of your teeth or shattered bones, radiation is utilised at low doses in x-rays to see inside your body.
 
• Radiation therapy damages cancer cells' DNA, which either kills them or limits their growth at high dosages.
 
• Cancer cells that have DNA damage that cannot be repaired either cease proliferating or die.
 
• When the injured cells expire, the body degrades and eliminates them.
 
• But too much radiation can damage tissues by changing cell structure and damaging DNA.
 
• This can cause serious health problems.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chemotherapy **

 
 
• Chemotherapy is the use of any drug to treat any disease.
 
• But to most people, the word chemotherapy means drugs used for** cancer treatment**. 
 
• It's often shortened to “chemo.” Surgery and radiation therapy remove, kill, or damage cancer cells in a certain area, but chemo can work throughout the whole body.
 
 

 
• Surgery:

 
 
• Surgery is a medical speciality that employs operative manual and instrumental techniques on a patient to examine or treat a pathological condition.
 
• Such as a disease or injury, to enhance bodily function or appearance, or to repair unwelcome ruptured areas
 
 
 
• **Physiotherapy**
 
 
• ​Physiotherapy is a healthcare profession that aims to help people restore and maintain movement and function when affected by** injury**, **illness** or **disability**.
 
• Physiotherapists use a combination of manual **therapy**, **exercise**, and **education**.

questions.question: Antonie van Leeuwenhoek was known for which discovery in late 17th century?

options.text: Discovery of the properties of a stem cell
Discovery of the role of ATP as the source of energy for cells
Discovery of nucleus in the cell

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Observation of bacteria and protozoa. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Leeuwenhoek is universally acknowledged as the father of microbiology. 
 
• He discovered both protists and bacteria.
 
• More than being the first to see this unimagined world of 'animalcules', he was the first even to think of looking—certainly, the first with the power to see.
 
• Antonie van Leeuwenhoek used single-lens microscopes, which he made, to make the first observations of bacteria and protozoa. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The key properties of a stem cell were first defined by Ernest McCulloch and James Till at the University of Toronto and the Ontario Cancer Institute in the early 1960s.​ 
 
• The ATP molecule was discovered in the year 1929 by German chemist Karl Lohmann.
 
• Robert Brown discovered the nucleus of the cell in 1804.

questions.question: How do humans acclimatise at high altitudes where atmospheric pressure is low for normal breathing?

options.text: By decreasing red blood cell production, decreasing the binding affinity of haemoglobin and by increasing breathing rate
By increasing red blood cell production, decreasing the binding affinity of haemoglobin and by increasing breathing rate
By increasing white blood cell production, decreasing the binding affinity of haemoglobin and by increasing breathing rate

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**By increasing red blood cell production, decreasing the binding affinity of haemoglobin and by increasing breathing rate**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Acclimatisation**

 
 
• **Acclimatisation** is the l**ong-term adaptation to high altitude**, which is primarily carried on **by an increase in red blood cell production and capillary tissue perfusion**.
 
• At high altitudes, acclimatisation typically **takes 1-3 days**.
 
• The b**ody undergoes a number of adaptations** that enable it to **function with less oxygen **at high altitudes, such as:
 
 
• the** depth of breathing increases **or by increasing breathing rate.
 
• Increased **pulmonary arterial pressure "forces" blood into areas of the lung** that are typically not used when breathing at sea level.
 
• The **body creates more red blood cells to transport oxygen**, as well as more of an enzyme. 
 
• By decreasing the **binding affinity of haemoglobin**.
 
 
 
• In order to reduce the **effects of altitude sickness and to balance out increased urination, it's critical to stay hydrated during acclimatisation**.
 
• Despite acclimation, the **heart rate and ventilation rate both rise when at rest, **whereas the heart rate falls when ** at its highest degree of activity due to the release of oxygen from haemoglobin to the body's tissues**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Altitude Sickness**

 
 
• At sea level, **there are around 21% more oxygen** molecules than usual.
 
• While the **concentration does not change with the increase in altitude but the amount of oxygen molecules per breath and the atmospheric pressure decreases**.
 
• At **12,000 feet (3,658 metres)**, there are around **40% less oxygen **molecules in each breath.
 
• Even while at rest, **your breathing rate needs to increase for the body to receive enough oxygen**.
 
• Continued exposure to **higher altitudes without enough acclimatisation might result in very serious, even fatal illnesses**.

questions.question: Which of the following is a variety of oilseed?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Taramira**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Taramira oil, commonly known as Jamba oil.
 
• Taramira oil is a seed oil, pressed from the seeds of the arugula.
 
• The plant of Tamaria oilseed is highly drought-resistant, the oil is popular in regions of poor rainfall, particularly in West Asia, Pakistan, and Northern India.
 
• Taramira seeds are oilseeds and are mostly used in cattle feed. 
 
• It is also used in hair oil and skincare products.

questions.question: Vitamin B Complex consists of how many vitamins?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**8**__.

__**Explanation:**__

__
 
• **The B complex consists of eight water-soluble vitamins that perform essential and closely related roles in the body's cellular function**__.
 
• These include thiamine (**vitamin B1**), riboflavin (**vitamin B2**), niacin (**vitamin B3**), pantothenic acid (**vitamin B5**), pyridoxine (**vitamin B6**), **biotin **(vitamin B7),** folic acid **(vitamin B9), and cobalamins (**vitamin B12**)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• B vitamins play a vital role in maintaining good health and well-being. As the building blocks of a healthy body, B vitamins have a direct impact on your energy levels, **brain function, and cell metabolism**.
 
• B vitamins are especially important for women who are pregnant and breastfeeding. These vitamins aid in fetal brain development as well as reduce the risk of birth defects.
 
• And for expectant mothers, B vitamins may boost energy levels, ease nausea, and **lower the risk of developing preeclampsia**.
 
• B vitamins are thought to increase testosterone levels in men, which naturally decrease with age. They may also help men build muscle and increase strength. However, human studies confirming these claims are lacking. 
 
• Each member of the B-complex has a unique structure and performs unique functions in the human body.
 
• **Vitamins B1, B2, B3, and biotin participate in different aspects of energy production, vitamin B6 is essential for amino acid metabolism, and vitamin B12 and folic acid facilitate steps required for cell division.**
